name: Kuwait International Airport
before:
Kuwait's airport, in Farwaniya Governorate 15.5 km south of central Kuwait City, and the hub for both Kuwait Airways and Jazeera Airways. As of 2025 it is the twelfth busiest in the Middle East.

The terminal situation needs checking before every booking. The airport is meant to have five numbered terminals in operation by 2026. Terminal 4 opened in August 2018 and is used only by Kuwait Airways. Terminal 2, a large Foster and Partners building with 28 gates and an airside hotel, has slipped repeatedly: it began construction in May 2017, was due in August 2022, was pushed to 2024 by the pandemic and is now targeted at the last quarter of 2026. Its construction site was struck by an Iranian drone, with minor damage reported and no change to that target.

So confirm the terminal with the airline rather than assuming, because the picture is still moving.

There are three runways, the longest 3,500 metres. Part of the complex is an air force base.
after:
Kuwait's airport, 15.5 km south of central Kuwait City, and the hub for both Kuwait Airways and Jazeera Airways.

Flights stopped on 28 February 2026, when Kuwait shut its airspace in the Iran war, and the two home airlines only restarted on 26 April. An air strike on 3 June badly damaged Terminal 1. In September it was still closed, and Terminals 4 and 5 were handling all flights on reduced schedules. The civil aviation authority also denied reports that transit flights would start on 1 October.

Airspace can still close at short notice, so check the terminal and the schedule with the airline before every booking.

A new Terminal 2 by Foster and Partners, under construction since May 2017, is due to be finished in late 2026. There are three runways, the longest 4,580 metres, and part of the complex is an air force base.
